intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians perform as the square transforms from a daytime market into a spectacular open-air food festival at dusk. Wander the labyrinthine souks of the ancient medina, haggling for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles just steps from your accommodation.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp in Merzouga
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for an unforgettable camel trek into the Sahara. Ride at sunset as the dunes glow amber and rose, then spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp under a canopy of stars. Enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake at dawn for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes — a once-in-a-lifetime desert experience.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back in time with a self-guided or local-guided tour of two of Marrakech's most significant historical landmarks. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with its intricate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. A short walk away, the Saadian Tombs — sealed for centuries and rediscovered in 1917 — house the ornate mausoleums of the Saadian dynasty, offering a profound glimpse into Morocco's imperial past.
experiences.location: Kasbah & Riad Zitoun districts, Medina, Marrakech

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class with a Local Family
experiences.description: Begin your morning at the vibrant Mellah spice market to hand-select fresh ingredients — saffron, ras el hanout, preserved lemons, and more. Then join a local Marrakchi family in their home kitchen to learn the art of preparing authentic dishes such as slow-cooked lamb tagine, harira soup, and honey-drenched bastilla. Sit down together to enjoy the feast you've created, paired with fresh-baked khobz bread and mint tea.

experiences.name: Ait Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Day Trip
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day excursion from Marrakech over the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Ait Benhaddou — a stunning fortified mud-brick village used as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, palm groves, and Berber villages, offering rich historical and cultural context to your Moroccan journey.
experiences.location: Ait Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late arrival day. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Take a petit taxi from Marrakech Menara Airport to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat (approx. 15–20 min, ~70–100 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at 22:30. After check-in, take a short stroll to the nearby Jemaa el-Fna square (5-min walk) to soak in the late-night atmosphere – street performers, food stalls, and the buzz of the medina. Keep it brief as it's late.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In transit
meals.lunch: N/A – In transit / airport food
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – try a bowl of harira soup (10–15 MAD) or a msemen flatbread (5 MAD). Budget: ~20–30 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Confirm hotel has 24-hour reception for late check-in. Exchange some currency at the airport (small amount) or use an ATM. Petit taxis are metered – insist on the meter or agree on a price beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then head to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (free, exterior only) for a peaceful morning walk and photos of the iconic minaret. Continue to the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning 19th-century palace with intricate tilework and carved ceilings, a must-see for history lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the adjacent Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) – 16th-century royal tombs with beautiful mosaic decoration. Wander through the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) for panoramic views and a sense of Marrakech's imperial past. These three sites are all within walking distance of each other.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna square at sunset to witness the magical transformation – snake charmers, storytellers, and dozens of food stalls firing up. Explore the souks branching off the square (Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices) for free browsing and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Café de France or a local café near Jemaa el-Fna – mint tea, msemen, and amlou (almond-argan dip). Budget: ~25–40 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack stand near Bahia Palace – kefta sandwich or merguez roll with harissa. Budget: ~20–30 MAD
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls (stall numbers 1–100) – try tangia, couscous, or grilled brochettes with bread. Budget: ~50–80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks but you're not obligated to buy. Carry small change for entrance fees. Total entrance fees today: ~210 MAD (~$21 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD) – one of the most beautiful Islamic schools in North Africa, with stunning stucco and zellige tilework. Explore the surrounding northern medina neighborhood, including the Mouassine Fountain and the Chrob ou Chouf Fountain (free). Browse the Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk) for colorful textile displays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Jardin Majorelle (entrance ~150 MAD for garden + Berber Museum) – the iconic cobalt-blue garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. It's a bit pricier but absolutely worth it for the visual experience and cultural exhibits. Alternatively, visit the free Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam nearby for a relaxing garden stroll if budget is tight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mouassine neighborhood in the evening – quieter than Jemaa el-Fna, with artisan workshops and local life. Visit a hammam for a traditional Moroccan bath experience. Budget hammams like Hammam Dar el-Bacha charge ~50–100 MAD for a basic session.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local bakery (hanout) near Derb Sidi Bouloukat – fresh khobz bread, olive oil, and tea. Budget: ~15–25 MAD
meals.lunch: Café Arabe or a local restaurant near Ben Youssef – vegetable tagine with bread. Budget: ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad Yima café or a local eatery in Mouassine – pastilla or zaalouk (eggplant salad) with bread. Budget: ~50–70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Jardin Majorelle is the biggest splurge of the day but highly recommended for culture and history enthusiasts. Book hammam in advance if possible. Today is a good day to buy any souvenirs – spices, argan oil, and leather goods are best purchased in the medina souks.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a shared group tour or budget CTM/Supratours bus to Ouarzazate or Merzouga. A budget shared minibus tour (booked through a local agency near Jemaa el-Fna) typically costs 250–400 MAD per person for a 2-day/1-night Sahara trip. The journey passes through the stunning Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains – breathtaking scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar/fortified village) – a free exterior visit or small entrance fee (~10 MAD). This ancient mud-brick citadel has been used as a film set for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Continue driving through the Draa Valley with its palm groves and kasbahs toward the desert.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara (Merzouga or Zagora depending on tour). Mount camels for a sunset ride into the dunes (included in most budget tours). Watch the sunset over the Erg Chebbi dunes – one of the most spectacular sights in Morocco. Overnight in a budget desert camp with dinner and traditional Berber music around a campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure – grab khobz and cheese from a local hanout near the hotel. Budget: ~15–20 MAD
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant stop en route (usually included or arranged by tour) – harira soup and tagine. Budget: ~50–80 MAD or included in tour
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp package – traditional Berber dinner (tagine, couscous, mint tea). Budget: included in tour price

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sahara tour 1–2 days in advance from agencies near Jemaa el-Fna. Compare prices from at least 3 agencies. A 2-day/1-night budget tour typically costs 400–700 MAD per person including transport, camel ride, camp accommodation, and meals. Bring warm layers – desert nights are cold in March (can drop to 5–10°C). Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (5:30 AM) to watch the sunrise over the Sahara dunes – an unforgettable experience. Take a morning walk or short camel ride through the dunes. Explore the local Berber village near the camp. Have breakfast at the camp (usually included).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech. Stop at the Todra Gorge (if the route allows) – dramatic 300m-high limestone canyon walls, free to walk through. Continue through the Roses Valley (Vallée des Roses) near Kelaat M'Gouna, famous for its Damask rose fields (in bloom in April–May, but still scenic in March). Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon/early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover at Hotel Aday after the long journey. Light evening stroll through the medina. Visit a local hammam for post-desert relaxation if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: Included in desert camp – Berber bread, olive oil, honey, mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route – tagine or sandwich. Budget: ~50–80 MAD or included in tour
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near Jemaa el-Fna – try tanjia Marrakchia (slow-cooked lamb, a Marrakech specialty) or a simple chicken tagine. Budget: ~60–90 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long (6–8 hours with stops). Stay hydrated and bring snacks for the road. If you feel adventurous, ask the tour driver to stop at any interesting roadside spots – flexibility is a perk of small group tours. Rest well tonight for the final days in Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Marrakech Museum (Musée de Marrakech, entrance ~50 MAD) housed in the beautiful Mnebhi Palace – exhibits on Moroccan art, ceramics, and manuscripts. Explore the nearby Almoravid Koubba (entrance ~20 MAD) – the only surviving Almoravid-era structure in Marrakech (12th century). Walk through the northern medina at a leisurely pace, observing daily local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a day trip or afternoon excursion to the Ourika Valley (30km from Marrakech) via a shared grand taxi (~30–40 MAD each way from Bab Rob). Enjoy the lush Berber villages, terraced gardens, and the Atlas Mountain backdrop. Walk to the Ourika waterfalls (small guide fee ~20–30 MAD). This is a refreshing contrast to the desert and city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech for a final evening in the medina. Visit the Mellah market for fresh produce, olives, and preserved lemons. Enjoy a rooftop café experience overlooking Jemaa el-Fna – many offer mint tea with views for ~20–30 MAD.

meals.breakfast: Local café near hotel – beghrir (semolina pancakes with honey and butter) and mint tea. Budget: ~25–35 MAD
meals.lunch: Ourika Valley – eat at a local Berber family restaurant along the river (tagine with mountain herbs). Budget: ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls or Café Clock (known for camel burger and cultural events) – Budget: ~60–100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Grand taxis to Ourika Valley depart from Bab Rob (southern gate of the medina). Negotiate the price before getting in. The valley can be muddy in March – wear appropriate footwear. Café Clock near the Koutoubia often hosts free or low-cost cultural events (storytelling, music) in the evenings – check their schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech – revisit your favorite spots in the medina at a relaxed pace. Browse the Sunday souk at Bab el-Khemis (flea market, free entry) for antiques, vintage items, and local crafts – great for last-minute budget souvenirs. Pick up spices (cumin, ras el hanout, saffron), argan oil, or leather goods as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Cyber Park or Menara Gardens (free) for a peaceful final afternoon – the Menara pavilion and olive grove reflect beautifully in the basin. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Check out of Hotel Aday (confirm checkout time). Head to the airport via petit taxi (~70–100 MAD) with plenty of time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert adventure, history, and local flavors in Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Final traditional Moroccan breakfast – msemen, amlou, fresh orange juice (Morocco is famous for its fresh-squeezed OJ, ~10 MAD a glass), and mint tea. Budget: ~30–45 MAD
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the medina – bissara (fava bean soup with olive oil and cumin, a Moroccan street food staple, ~15–20 MAD) and khobz bread. Budget: ~25–35 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight (departure day)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the taxi ride and airport security. Marrakech Menara Airport is small but can get busy. Spend any remaining dirhams on airport snacks or last-minute gifts – dirhams cannot easily be converted outside Morocco. Total estimated daily budget (excluding tours): 200–350 MAD/day (~$20–35 USD) for food and local transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or a petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat, located in the heart of the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a feel for the riad-style surroundings. If still hungry, grab a light snack from a nearby street stall in Jemaa el-Fna square (a 5-minute walk).

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night street food at Jemaa el-Fna – try a bowl of harira soup and msemen flatbread from the food stalls (~30–50 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance since arrival is late. Exchange some currency at the airport (ATMs available). The Medina streets can be narrow and confusing at night – ask hotel staff to guide you or meet you nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then explore the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive. Walk to the Koutoubia Mosque (exterior view) and stroll through the surrounding gardens. Head into the souks – explore Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices (Spice Market), and the dyers' quarter for an authentic sensory experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century riad-palace with ornate Moroccan architecture and lush gardens. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and browse the antique shops and local stalls. Stop at Place des Ferblantiers for a rest and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant open-air spectacle – snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and dozens of food stalls. Dine at one of the numbered food stalls in the square for a classic Marrakech experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café des Épices near the spice market – mint tea, msemen, honey, and amlou (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Bahia Palace – try a chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~60–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – you'll cover 5–8 km on foot. Beware of unofficial 'guides' in the souks who may lead you to shops for commission. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis. Then head to the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) for sweeping views of Marrakech and fascinating history of the Saadian dynasty. Explore the stork nests on the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum complex (garden entry ~150 MAD, museum ~100 MAD). Wander through the cobalt-blue villa and exotic botanical garden co-restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Afterward, explore the Gueliz (Nouvelle Ville) neighborhood for a change of pace – modern cafés, art galleries, and boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Gueliz at a mid-range restaurant. Return to the Medina by petit taxi and take an evening walk along the illuminated ramparts near Bab Agnaou gate.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery – fresh khobz bread, olive oil, and coffee (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café Kif Kif or similar near Majorelle Garden – Moroccan salads, pastilla, and fresh juice (~100–150 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Gueliz – try pastilla au pigeon (sweet-savory pigeon pie) or lamb mechoui (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden gets crowded by midday – aim to arrive around 14:00 after the lunch rush. Book YSL Museum tickets online in advance if possible. March weather in Marrakech is mild (~18–24°C), perfect for garden visits.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (07:00) from Marrakech by private shared transfer or rented car toward the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley route. Drive through the High Atlas Mountains, crossing the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at a roadside Berber café for tea and views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate – stop briefly to see the Taourirt Kasbah (entry ~20 MAD), a UNESCO-listed earthen fortress. Drive onward through the Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs and the Draa Valley palm groves toward Zagora or Merzouga (depending on chosen desert destination). Arrive at your desert camp or guesthouse by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute ride into the Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes. Watch the sun set over the Sahara from the top of a dune. Settle into a traditional Berber desert camp for the night under a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure (~40–60 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant near Ouarzazate – harira, tagine, and Moroccan bread (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp – vegetable couscous, tagine, Moroccan salads, and mint tea (~150–200 MAD, often included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~8–10 hours total with stops). Book a shared transfer or private driver in advance (~600–900 MAD per person shared, or ~1,500–2,000 MAD for a private car). Desert camp accommodation ranges from 400–800 MAD per person for a mid-range luxury tent with private bathroom. Bring a warm layer – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 06:00) to climb the dunes and watch the sunrise over the Sahara – one of the most breathtaking experiences in Morocco. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Explore the surrounding dunes on foot or by quad bike (optional, ~200–300 MAD). Visit a nearby Berber village to learn about nomadic desert life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech or stop overnight in the Dades Valley. If returning, drive through the stunning Dades Gorge and Todra Gorge (a narrow canyon with 300m-high walls) – allow 1–2 hours for a walk through the gorge. Continue toward the Rose Valley (Vallée des Roses), famous for its Damask rose fields (peak bloom in April–May, but still scenic in March).
day_by_day.evening: Overnight in a mid-range guesthouse (maison d'hôte) in the Dades Valley or Boumalne Dades. Enjoy a quiet evening in a traditional Berber home setting.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at desert camp – msemen, argan oil, honey, dates, and mint tea (included in camp)
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in Tinghir near Todra Gorge – tagine and fresh salad (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner in Dades Valley – slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds (~120–160 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge walk is easy and suitable for all fitness levels. The gorge is narrowest and most dramatic in the first 300 meters. If you prefer to return directly to Marrakech, it's possible but makes for a very long day (10+ hours driving). Splitting the return over two days is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Morning walk in the Dades Valley among the kasbahs and almond/walnut orchards. Visit the Aït Benhaddou Ksar on the return route – this UNESCO World Heritage earthen citadel has been used as a filming location for Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia (entry ~10 MAD, guide recommended at ~100–150 MAD). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the multi-level ksar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive back over the Tizi n'Tichka pass toward Marrakech. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon (~17:00–18:00). Check back into Hotel Aday and freshen up. Visit a traditional hammam for a relaxing steam bath and scrub – try Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a local neighborhood hammam (~50–150 MAD depending on services).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the Medina. Enjoy a final stroll through Jemaa el-Fna and pick up last-minute souvenirs – argan oil, saffron, leather goods, or Berber rugs.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Dades Valley – bread, olive oil, honey, and coffee (included or ~40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch near Aït Benhaddou – Berber omelette, tagine, and fresh-squeezed juice at a local café (~80–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Marrakech Medina – try b'stilla (seafood or chicken), lamb tagine with ras el hanout, and Moroccan pastries for dessert (~180–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Aït Benhaddou is best visited in the morning before tour buses arrive. The ksar requires crossing a shallow river (stepping stones available) or a small footbridge. Hammam visits should be booked in advance for private sessions. Tipping the hammam attendant 20–30 MAD is customary.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech – visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century palace, featuring Moroccan art, ceramics, and manuscripts. Explore the nearby Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellige tilework and carved stucco – one of the finest examples of Moroccan architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks – focus on the leather souk (Souk Cherratine) and the carpet souk for authentic Moroccan crafts. Enjoy a final mint tea ceremony at a traditional café. Pack up at the hotel and arrange airport transfer (allow 30–45 minutes to the airport, more during busy periods).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert adventure, history, and unforgettable Moroccan flavors.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or Café des Épices – avocado toast Moroccan-style, mint tea, and fresh orange juice (~50–80 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a souk café or riad restaurant – Moroccan lentil soup, zaalouk (eggplant salad), and khobz bread (~70–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or early dinner before departure – grab a final pastry (cornes de gazelle) and coffee (~30–50 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Madrasa and the Musée de Marrakech are within walking distance of each other and close to the hotel – ideal for a final morning. Check out time is typically 12:00; ask the hotel to store luggage if your flight is later. Keep 100–200 MAD in cash for tips, taxis, and small purchases on the last day. Marrakech airport is small – arrive 2 hours before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Hotel Aday in the heart of the Medina (Derb Sidi Bouloukat). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea and light snack prepared by the riad staff. Settle into your suite and rest after the journey.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter of Moroccan mezze and pastilla bites arranged by the riad — dates, olives, harissa, and warm khobz bread served in your room or private courtyard

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Hotel Aday is a boutique riad — the narrow Medina lanes require a local guide or tuk-tuk for the final approach from the drop-off point. Keep luggage manageable for the last 100m walk through the derb (alley).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast on the riad rooftop terrace. At 10:00, begin a private guided walking tour of the Medina — explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive, then wind through the historic souks: spice market (Rahba Kedima), leather tanneries viewpoint, and the dyers' souk. Visit the 14th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most stunning examples of Moorish architecture in North Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, visit the Bahia Palace (Palais de la Bahia) — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with ornate tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Continue to the Saadian Tombs, a royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered only in 1917. End the afternoon with a private calligraphy or zellige tile-making workshop arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back through Djemaa el-Fna at dusk as the square transforms — snake charmers, storytellers, and food stalls ignite the night. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails (or fresh-pressed juices) at a rooftop terrace bar overlooking the square. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Riad rooftop breakfast — msemen (flaky flatbread), amlou (argan oil & almond dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan mint tea, honey, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjan, Medina) — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views; try the lamb pastilla and harira soup
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk (55 Souk Hal Fassi) — a beautifully restored 18th-century caravanserai serving refined Moroccan-French cuisine; reserve the mezzanine for the best ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Book Ben Youssef Madrasa tickets in advance — timed entry recommended. Private guide for the morning souk walk enhances the experience significantly and helps avoid tourist traps. Dress modestly for religious and historical sites.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Majorelle Garden — the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, now home to the Berber Museum (Musée Berbère). Arrive at opening (09:00) to enjoy it before the midday crowds. Explore the YSL Memorial and the adjacent MIAM (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech) for a fascinating intersection of fashion, art, and Moroccan culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class at a premium culinary atelier in the Medina (such as La Maison Arabe Cooking School or Souk Cuisine). Learn to prepare a traditional Moroccan feast: harira soup, chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives, couscous with seven vegetables, and bastilla au lait for dessert. This is a hands-on, immersive 3-hour experience with a local chef.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam and spa experience at a luxury hammam (such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Royal Mansour Spa if accessible). Enjoy a traditional black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Return to the riad refreshed for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast — beghrir (semolina pancakes with honey butter), soft-boiled eggs, fresh fruit platter, and Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — a convivial lunch with your instructor and fellow guests in a traditional Moroccan dining room
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout (79 Sidi Ahmed Soussi) — a legendary Marrakech institution set in a stunning riad; multi-course Moroccan feast with live Gnawa music; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden tickets sell out — book online at least 48 hours ahead. The YSL Museum requires a separate ticket. Hammam sessions should be booked 24 hours in advance. Dar Yacout is one of Marrakech's most celebrated dining experiences — dress elegantly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at 07:00 by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the journey to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). The route crosses the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) — stop for photos at the summit and visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (fortified village), a breathtaking 11th-century earthen citadel that has served as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Private guided tour of the ksar included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley and the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) — a stunning gorge lined with rose bushes, kasbahs, and palm groves. Stop at a local cooperative to learn about rose water and argan oil production. Pass through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') and continue toward the desert. Arrive at your luxury desert camp or kasbah hotel near Merzouga by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount your camel at sunset for a guided ride into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi — the most spectacular sand sea in Morocco, with dunes reaching 150m. Watch the sunset from the top of a dune with a glass of Moroccan tea. Overnight at a premium luxury desert camp (private ensuite tent with real beds, electricity, and hot showers).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure — packed travel breakfast if needed
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — traditional Berber tagine and fresh salads with Atlas Mountain views
meals.dinner: Dinner under the stars at the luxury desert camp — traditional Moroccan feast around a fire pit with live Berber music (guembri and bendir drums); menu includes mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous, and Saharan mint tea ceremony

day_by_day.notes: The Marrakech–Merzouga drive is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — an early departure is essential. Alternatively, a scenic flight to Ouarzazate can shorten the journey (check availability). Pack a light jacket — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private sunrise hike to the top of the highest dune in Erg Chebbi — an unforgettable experience as the Sahara turns from deep purple to blazing gold. Return to camp for a leisurely Berber breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a 4x4 desert excursion to visit a nomadic Berber family in their traditional tent — share tea and learn about their way of life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the desert camp and visit the Merzouga village and the shores of Dayet Srji — a seasonal salt lake that attracts flamingos in spring (March is an excellent time). Visit a local fossil and mineral workshop — the Sahara region is world-famous for its trilobite and ammonite fossils. Begin the return journey westward, stopping at the Todra Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300m-high rose-colored limestone walls, perfect for a scenic walk along the river.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a luxury kasbah hotel in the Draa Valley or Skoura oasis for the night (such as Kasbah Bab Ourika or Dar Ahlam if routing allows). Enjoy a private terrace dinner overlooking a palm grove.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — khobz, olive oil, honey, argan amlou, hard-boiled eggs, fresh mint tea, and dates
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the camp — Moroccan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and juice enjoyed at the Todra Gorge riverside
meals.dinner: Dinner at your kasbah hotel — refined Moroccan cuisine featuring local specialties such as lamb with prunes and almonds, served in a candlelit courtyard

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise dune climb is the highlight of the Sahara experience — do not miss it. Wear closed shoes for the dune walk. The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the late afternoon light. Confirm your kasbah hotel booking well in advance as luxury properties in the valley have limited rooms.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the kasbah — optional yoga session on the rooftop or a guided walk through the palmery (palm grove oasis). Depart after breakfast and continue the return journey to Marrakech via the scenic Ourika Valley route or the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Stop at a traditional Berber argan oil cooperative run by women — learn about the labor-intensive process of hand-cracking argan nuts and purchase authentic cold-pressed argan oil directly from the source.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday. Spend the afternoon on a curated luxury shopping experience in the Medina souks with a private guide — focus on high-quality artisan goods: hand-knotted Berber rugs, silver jewelry, hand-painted ceramics, bespoke leather babouches (slippers), and pure argan oil products. Visit a reputable fixed-price artisan cooperative to avoid bargaining stress.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar with panoramic Medina views (Sky Bar at the Selman Hotel or Kabana Rooftop). Final evening in Marrakech — a special farewell dinner at one of the city's most prestigious restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the kasbah — a lavish spread of local cheeses, honey, msemen, fresh-squeezed juices, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route — stop at a roadside café in the Atlas foothills for a simple but authentic harira soup and Moroccan salads
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at La Mamounia's Le Marocain restaurant — the most iconic luxury dining experience in Marrakech, set in the legendary La Mamounia palace hotel; traditional Moroccan cuisine elevated to haute cuisine; full evening dress recommended

day_by_day.notes: La Mamounia's Le Marocain requires advance reservation and smart dress code. The return drive from the desert is approximately 5–6 hours — plan accordingly. The argan cooperative visit is best arranged through your hotel or guide to ensure authenticity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow breakfast on the riad rooftop. Take a peaceful early morning walk through the Medina before the souks open — the narrow alleys are magical in the quiet morning light. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (the mosque exterior and gardens are open to non-Muslims) — the 12th-century minaret is the architectural inspiration for the Giralda in Seville and the Hassan Tower in Rabat. Last-minute souvenir shopping or a final mint tea at a traditional café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: optional visit to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the Lazama Synagogue — a fascinating and often-overlooked layer of Marrakech's multicultural history. Check out of Hotel Aday and arrange private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Carry the memories of the Sahara, the souks, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — a leisurely spread of all your Moroccan favorites: msemen, beghrir, amlou, fresh orange juice, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices (75 Rahba Lakdima, Place des Épices) — a beloved Medina institution with rooftop terrace views over the spice square; try the zaalouk, briouats, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with Hotel Aday — standard checkout is typically 12:00 but late checkout may be arranged for a premium. Keep a small amount of Moroccan dirhams for tips and last-minute purchases. Marrakech airport can be busy — arrive early. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if returning to the EU or US.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March
